decisive_items: Localized tenderness and rebound pain in the right lower abdomen
response.rationale: Intestinal obstruction is the most likely diagnosis due to the combination of abdominal pain, vomiting, and radiographic evidence of dilated bowel and air-fluid levels. While bowel ischemia is also a possible diagnosis, the presence of thickened intestinal wall and dense tubular shadows in the narrow lumen are not exclusive to ischemia and can also be seen in obstruction.

rejected.why: Internal hernia is possible but less likely due to the lack of specific imaging findings supporting this diagnosis
Gastrointestinal perforation is possible but the presence of free gas under the diaphragm and pneumatosis in the abdominal cavity can also be seen in other conditions
Gastrointestinal fistula is less likely due to the lack of specific imaging findings supporting this diagnosis
